analysis.hypothesis: Implement element-wise sigmoid and InstanceNorm2d (affine=False) as separate CUDA kernels in kernels/custom_ops.cu, with launchers exposing raw pointers and stream. Sigmoid kernel processes all elements using input strides for non-contiguous support. InstanceNorm kernel launches one thread per (N,C) instance, each computes mean/variance over spatial dims using strides, then normalizes all spatial elements. These kernels together should match reference semantics and be faster than torch.compile via custom CUDA.

analysis.hypothesis: The illegal memory access in custom_sigmoid is caused by passing host pointers for in_strides/out_strides/shape to the CUDA kernel, because the binding code incorrectly reinterprets int64_t arrays as int* and passes them to the kernel without copying to device memory.
evidence: In custom_ops_binding.cpp, in_strides, out_strides, and shape are declared as int64_t arrays on the host stack.
The launcher signature expects const int* pointers, but the binding passes reinterpret_cast<int*>(in_strides), which points to host memory.
Inside the kernel, these pointers are dereferenced as device pointers (in_strides[d], shape[d]), causing an illegal memory access.
The sanitizer log indicates the crash occurs inside custom_sigmoid_kernel, consistent with accessing invalid memory addresses.
No device-side arrays are allocated or copied for these metadata, so all kernel accesses to them are invalid.
